name: Chromatic Colophon
description: Chromatic Colophon marks the outer boundary of a densely populated star system, its enormous bulk serving as both gravitational anchor and navigational landmark for vessels entering or leaving the system's busy shipping lanes. Its atmosphere displays an extraordinary range of colors—deep indigo at the poles, bands of jade and copper through the mid-latitudes, and a churning equatorial zone of crimson and gold where opposing wind systems collide at hypersonic speeds. The visual effect is of a living artwork, constantly shifting but never repeating.

The toxic atmosphere is rich in complex hydrocarbons that create the vivid coloration, and the storm systems that churn through these chemical layers produce lightning displays of staggering scale and frequency. A planet-spanning hurricane at the southern pole has been stable for at least three centuries of observation, its interior layers spiraling through the full visible spectrum as different chemical compounds are drawn into its circulation. The orbital debris ring is thin but extensive, casting delicate shadow lines across the upper atmosphere during the system's brief eclipses.

An automated navigation beacon has orbited Chromatic Colophon for over two hundred years, guiding vessels through the transition between inner-system traffic patterns and outer-system transit corridors. The beacon's logs contain a comprehensive record of every vessel that has passed through the system during that period—an inadvertent archive of commerce, migration, and conflict. Historians have begun petitioning for access to the older log entries, which cover a period of political upheaval whose records were otherwise destroyed.

Chromatic Colophon's helium-3 reserves are commercially significant but difficult to extract due to the toxic atmospheric chemistry and violent storm activity. Several mining platforms have been proposed, and one was briefly operational before a hurricane migration pattern shift destroyed it. The planet remains more valuable as a waypoint than a resource—the colophon at the end of every journey through this system, marking the boundary between the known and the vast darkness beyond.
